# wtho.art — Thorsten Weitz

> Studio site of Thorsten Weitz, painter in Freiburg, Germany. Practice: synthetic expressionism — oil and mixed media on canvas and HDF. Series include “The feeling of…” and “Raw power and sensitivity”. Works are available on request.

Preferred name: Thorsten Weitz
Studio: Freiburg, Germany
Email: Wtho.Art@proton.me
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/wtho.art

## Site
- [Homepage](https://wtho.art/): Artist, studio, works, exhibitions, contact
- [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/wtho.art): Process and new paintings
- [Biography & Journey](https://wtho.art/images/portrait/): Thorsten Weitz (*1978) began his artistic journey in 1995. His early works were characterised by a fascination with the feminine and the expressive intensity of human eyes. Even his very first works immediately found buyers and patrons in and around Nördlingen – an early success that underlined the fundamental potential of his visual language. Nevertheless, he initially chose to pursue a career in education and worked as a teacher for many years. Alongside his teaching career, art remained his constant companion: occasional exhibitions and sales of his work punctuated his journey. At the same time, he deepened his work in the educational and artistic spheres through training in nature, rhythm and theatre education, as well as becoming a teacher of intuitive archery. “For me, the canvas has always been a space where movement, nature and human expression converge. During my years as an educator and performer, I learnt how intensely space and presence interact with and influence one another.” — Thorsten Weitz The years 2016–2020 demanded a fundamental reorientation – marked by profound personal upheavals, the transformation of familiar family structures leading to separation as a father of three children, health setbacks and the loss of previous certainties. The years 2016–2020 called for a fundamental reorientation – marked by profound personal turning points, the transformation of familiar family structures into separation as the father of three children, health setbacks, and the loss of previous certainties. “When familiar foundations crumble and you have to reorient yourself existentially, only the essential remains. For me, the canvas became the place where the force, the pain and the unshakeable courage to make a fresh start took on a visible form.” — Thorsten Weitz These phases of letting go and unconditional self-acceptance led him to the bodywork practices of Lomi Lomi and Qigong – the sensing of physical resonance – as well as to a deeper exploration of and apprenticeship in the Sweet Medicine philosophy of North and South America. They laid the foundation for his current artistic approach. In 2024, he made the resolute decision to place fine art squarely at the centre of his life and to realise his heart’s vision. His work is deeply influenced by the Sweet Medicine shamanic path from Arizona. The philosophy of the 20 primordial forces of the universe, as well as the principle of radical self-responsibility, flow directly into his painting process. “We are the cause of everything we experience. This realisation calls for an honest attitude towards one’s own being – and it is reflected on the canvas: my works are a constant balancing act between masculine and feminine forces, a dance of the elements and a struggle for inner balance.” — Thorsten Weitz Today, the works of this Freiburg-based artist bring together these diverse life experiences into a mature, powerful form of Synthetic Expressionism: a dynamic interplay of controlled chaos and pure energy. His paintings are not merely aesthetic objects, but spaces of energetic resonance for transformation.
- [Studio](https://wtho.art/images/atelier/): Where life and art merge inseparably. Thorsten Weitz’s studio is far more than just a place of creation or a workshop – it is the very centre of his life. Here, there is no distinction between everyday life and painting. Every thought, every vibration and the raw energy of daily existence flow directly and unfiltered into the creative process. In this space, the ethos of Synthetic Expressionism takes shape: The dynamic force and unpredictability of life are captured, reflected upon and translated into a clear form on the canvas. Life in the studio means constant movement, focused stillness and the creation of a tangible presence in every single work. “My studio is not a place I go to work. It is the space in which I live – and every canvas is the direct echo of this movement.” — Thorsten Weitz Studio visits for collectors and gallery owners: The impact of large-format oil paintings is felt most powerfully where they are created. Collectors, art lovers and gallery owners are warmly invited to visit the studio by prior appointment to experience the works in their original setting and through personal conversation.
- [Commissions & Residencies](https://wtho.art/images/commissions/): London: London is an example on this page. This text can be replaced in the studio. Commissions and residencies each have their own text and their own pictures. The pictures sit on the left and the text on the right.
